basic_info.name: Meu SUS Digital + RNDS (Brazilian Ministry of Health — national citizen health app + Rede Nacional de Dados em Saude, the national health data network)
basic_info.category: Government / public-sector digital health (national EHR exchange backbone + free citizen-facing records viewer)
basic_info.stage: Public, mature and actively expanding: app renamed from Conecte SUS to Meu SUS Digital (Jan 2024, per Portaria framework from 2020); RNDS formally instituted as the official SUS data-integration base with CPF as the single patient key by presidential decree signed 23-Jul-2025
basic_info.pricing_model: Free, taxpayer-funded, no ads, no paid tier, no upsell — zero price is structural and permanent. Nothing to monetize on the citizen side; there will never be a price increase because there is no price
basic_info.target_user: Entire Brazilian population using the public SUS (~170M+ potential users); in practice a broad low/middle-income base. Health professionals get a separate surface (SUS Digital Profissional); managers get SUS Digital Gestor (three-platform formalization per the 2025 decree)
basic_info.scale_metrics: Meu SUS Digital: 59M downloads and 29M users active in the last month (figures disclosed by the Health Ministry at the decree signing, July 2025). RNDS at that date: 21 states + Federal District integrated, 3,800+ municipalities sending data regularly, 2.8 billion accumulated clinical records — ~75M exam records, 436M encounters/attendances, 30.2M prescriptions dispensed, 9M hospitalizations (vaccine-record count reported as 1.5M by secondary source SBIS, likely a transcription of a much larger figure — treat that one number as unreliable). Assessment: this is durable national infrastructure, not hype; as a 'threat' it is a free baseline viewer, not a competing product — no retention loop, no interpretation, no monetization pressure

product.core_features: Today (verified via MS/RNDS official pages and Wikipedia, 2024-2026): (1) citizen clinical history — encounters/attendances, hospitalizations, dispensed medications; (2) national vaccination record + printable COVID certificate; (3) laboratory test results pushed to RNDS — formal scope of the REL standard is COVID-19 and mpox results from any clinical-analysis lab (public or private), with broader historic results appearing when state/municipal systems (e-SUS, GAL) feed the network; (4) digital SUS card / CADSUS; (5) real-time citizen support channel added 2024; (6) AI/predictive analytics for public-health management announced 2023 [uncertain: current live scope]; telemedicine module announced 2023 [uncertain: never confirmed live]. Login = gov.br account (CPF)
product.signature_differentiator: The only nationwide, legally mandated health record. Decree of 23-Jul-2025 (Decreto ~12.560 [uncertain: exact number truncated in sources]) makes RNDS the official SUS data base, adopts CPF as the single universal patient identifier across public and private care, and adds a financial lever: private providers only receive federal reimbursement (tax offset / debt settlement) for SUS services if those services are recorded in RNDS. No private player can replicate the legal mandate, the CPF key, or the reimbursement leverage — this is the moat, and it is the state's moat, not a product moat
product.lab_data_handling: Pure read-only display of results that laboratories push into RNDS. The REL (Resultado de Exame Laboratorial) standard is fully specified and verified: FHIR R4 Bundle type=document containing four profiles — Composition (BRRNDS document type 'REL'), Condition (diagnostic suspicion, CID-10), Observation (the result: quantitative valueQuantity+interpretation or qualitative valueCodeableConcept from BRResultadoQualitativoExame), Specimen (sample type, BRTipoAmostraGAL). Private labs MUST use LOINC exclusively for test codes (public may use GAL tables); collection datetime with timezone; result substitution via relatesTo/replaces. Critical scope fact: REL today formally covers SARS-CoV-2 and orthopoxvirus/mpox tests only, 'with planned expansion' to other pathogens. What is absent: no PDF upload, no patient-side ingestion, no interpretation, no reference-range flagging for citizens, no trends, no retest cadence, no hardware/wearables, no CGM, nothing annual-and-proactive — it is a mailbox for lab output, not a lab-data product
product.family_dependents_depth: Essentially none. Records are keyed 1:1 to CPF; a legal representative (e.g., parent of a minor) can access via their gov.br login [uncertain: exact representative flow details unverified]. No family dashboard, no caregiver mode, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary-risk view, no dependent switching. This remains the gap nobody in Brazil fills — same as the US finding
product.doctor_sharing: One-directional and intra-SUS only: professionals with SUS Digital Profissional can view the patient's RNDS history during care. There is no mechanism to package/share a summary with a private doctor, no exportable brief, no SOAP, no PDF for consultation, no link sharing. The patient's private physician sees nothing unless they are inside SUS
product.action_loop_monetization: None exists. The 'loop' after viewing a result is: go to a SUS unit. Government-side action loops are real though: Health Minister Padilha reported 150k+ people resumed Farmacia Popular treatments in June 2025 after cell-phone alerts triggered by RNDS data (patients who had not picked up medication). No supplements, no protocols marketplace, no telemedicine upsell, no prescriptions, no imaging/MCED marketplace — zero commercial action-loop design

technology.ai_approach: No patient-facing AI of any kind — no chatbot, no interpretation, no risk scoring for individuals. Backend predictive analytics for epidemic monitoring, outbreak early warning and resource optimization announced in 2023 [uncertain: how much is actually deployed vs announced]. For a patient, Meu SUS Digital is dumb storage with a UI; intelligence lives with managers, not citizens
technology.data_inputs: Institutional feeds only: e-SUS APS (primary care encounters), GAL/laboratory systems (REL results), immunization systems (RIA model), medication dispensation (Farmacia Popular / REDFM model — active FHIR IG updated Jul-2026), hospital systems (federal AGHU integrated to SUS Digital Jul-2025), clinical encounters (RAC model), care regulation (RIRA model). Zero patient-generated data: no PDFs, no wearables, no genomics, no questionnaires, no CGM, no Health Connect
technology.data_interoperability: The strongest in-country stack and the key strategic fact for Dr. Exame. RNDS = FHIR R4 national exchange with published BRRNDS profiles (REL exams, RIA immunization, RAC encounters, REDFM dispensation, RIRA regulation); implementation guides actively maintained on GitHub with updates as recent as Jul-2026. CPF is now the universal join key (2025 decree). Ingestion surface for citizens: NONE (no upload path). Exhaustion surface for third parties: none public — RNDS access requires establishment adhesion (gestor + integrator roles via DATASUS services portal); there is no citizen-consent API for private apps today [uncertain]. Private-sector track (Open Health/ANS): the ANS Open Health program page no longer exists at its former gov.br URL and the agency's Feb-2026 news feed shows no Open Health items — the program's original norms (RN 11/2024-era, FHIR-based operator-to-authorized-app data sharing with beneficiary consent) [uncertain: norm numbers, phase deadlines, and whether the program was renamed, folded into TISS 4, or paused] — while the operative private interoperability track is TISS 4 (FHIR migration, security/LGPD requirements; SBIS seminar Oct-2025) and a national interoperability maturity survey by ABCIS/HL7 Brasil/SBIS running Sep-2025 into Feb-2026
technology.platform: Android + iOS app (gov.br SSO) and web SPA at meususdigital.saude.gov.br; professional and manager portals separate

ux.onboarding: gov.br account (CPF + password/biometrics) then immediate access to whatever exists in RNDS for that CPF. Time-to-value is instant IF the citizen's municipality/lab feeds RNDS — vaccination card is the reliable first hit. Friction points: gov.br account level requirements and wildly uneven data completeness by region [uncertain: no first-hand app test performed; based on documented flow and user-reported patterns]
ux.data_visualization: Registry views: lists of vaccine doses with dates, encounter history, medication pickups, exam results shown as documents/records. No trends, no time-series charts, no reference-range comparison, no flags, no scores, no graphs [uncertain: exact 2026 UI details — app ships frequent updates; the absence-of-interpretation pattern is structural and confirmed]
ux.engagement_channel: Government push campaigns (vaccination drives, medication-pickup alerts — the 150k-resumption case) and news-driven spikes. Usage is transactional: citizen opens app when told to or to fetch a certificate. No community, no streaks, no habit loops. Retention = state campaigns, not product mechanics

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Not applicable in the consumer-app sense: it displays official records rather than interpreting them, so there are no accuracy claims, no methodology, no clinical board, no disclaimers needed. Trust derives from being the state. Known weakness is data completeness (results missing when labs/municipalities are not integrated) — a credibility risk of omission, not of error. Radical transparency of a different kind: the 2025 decree publishes record volumes publicly
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: It IS the regulator's own stack. LGPD-native (access restricted to assistance and management purposes; PII controls at national scale). The 2025 decree formalizes the three SUS Digital platforms and the CPF key. For Dr. Exame the regulatory reading is: (a) the state is standardizing FHIR R4 + LOINC + CPF as the national rails — every year the plumbing for a private interpretation layer gets better; (b) ANVISA SaMD (RDC 657/2022) pressure does not apply to a records viewer, and equally the state is NOT occupying the interpretation lane — the non-diagnosis posture Dr. Exame adopts is mirrored by the state's own app doing zero interpretation; (c) Open Health/ANS as originally framed (RN 11/2024-era, operator data to consented third-party apps) [uncertain: current legal status — program page removed from ANS site as of Aug-2026; TISS 4 is the live track] would, if/when enforced, hand private apps a standardized ingestion path into plan/lab data — the single biggest regulatory tailwind to watch
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What it does NOT do (the opportunity): zero interpretation of any value; no trends/longitudinal view; no reference-range comparison or flag education; no family/dependents layer; no caregiver mode; no doctor brief or sharing to private care; no PDF ingestion for the exams it does not receive; no AI chat; no action loop; REL formal scope still COVID/mpox — routine metabolic panels from private labs largely do not flow there (breadth depends on municipal GAL feeds). What works (inspiration, not copy): universal CPF identity = zero onboarding identity friction; vaccination card with shareable certificate is the killer feature that drove 59M downloads; state-scale push channel changes behavior (150k treatment resumptions). Strategic use for Dr. Exame: (1) today — Meu SUS Digital trains the entire population to expect exam results on a phone, then leaves them alone with unexplained numbers; Dr. Exame is the layer that explains, trends and prepares the doctor visit; (2) near-term — free marketing hook: 'got your result from Meu SUS? upload/PDF it here to understand it'; (3) long-term — if citizen-consented RNDS/Open Health-style access ever opens to private apps, REL/FHIR structured data replaces PDF OCR for a large share of ingest, and Dr. Exame should be positioned as the first consumer interpretation client on those rails
trust_gaps.relevance: High. Not a competitor — a free, non-retentive viewer with no interpretation and no action loop. Its relevance to Dr. Exame is threefold: (1) it normalizes digital exam results nationally (market education at zero cost); (2) it is the probable future structured ingestion source (FHIR R4/LOINC/CPF rails already built, REL scope expansion + any Open Health revival are the triggers to monitor quarterly); (3) its blind spots — interpretation, trends, family, doctor brief — are precisely Dr. Exame's pillars
